statement: The function returns a result r, and, with n = len(initial), m = len(target), and L defined as the largest natural number such that there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i, i + L <= n, 0 <= j, j + L <= m, and initial[i+t] = target[j+t] for every t with 0 <= t < L (the case L = 0 is allowed), the integer value of r is n + m - 2*L. Equivalently, r is the minimum number of single-character additions or removals at the beginning or end of initial needed to obtain target.
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail: no panic, out-of-bounds access, or 64-bit arithmetic overflow occurs.
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the integer value of r satisfies |len(initial) - len(target)| <= r <= len(initial) + len(target).
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a natural number L with 0 <= L <= min(len(initial), len(target)) such that r = len(initial) + len(target) - 2*L; equivalently, len(initial) + len(target) - r is even and its half lies between 0 and min(len(initial), len(target)).
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 0 if and only if len(initial) = len(target) and initial[i] = target[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(initial).
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = len(initial) + len(target) if and only if there is no byte value occurring in both initial and target, i.e. for every i with 0 <= i < len(initial) and every j with 0 <= j < len(target), initial[i] != target[j].
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = |len(initial) - len(target)| if and only if one of the two slices is a contiguous substring of the other: either there exists j with 0 <= j and j + len(target) <= len(initial) and initial[j+t] = target[t] for every t with 0 <= t < len(target), or there exists i with 0 <= i and i + len(initial) <= len(target) and target[i+t] = initial[t] for every t with 0 <= t < len(initial).
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every positive integer k and indices i and j such that 0 <= i, i + k <= len(initial), 0 <= j, j + k <= len(target), and initial[i+t] = target[j+t] for every t with 0 <= t < k, the integer value of r satisfies r <= len(initial) + len(target) - 2*k.
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, letting L = (len(initial) + len(target) - r)/2 (which is a natural number for every returned r), there exist indices i and j such that 0 <= i, i + L <= len(initial), 0 <= j, j + L <= len(target), and initial[i+t] = target[j+t] for every t with 0 <= t < L.
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, letting L = (len(initial) + len(target) - r)/2, there is no common contiguous substring of initial and target of length greater than L: for every positive integer k and indices i and j with 0 <= i, i + k <= len(initial), 0 <= j, j + k <= len(target), and initial[i+t] = target[j+t] for every t with 0 <= t < k, we have k <= L.
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: For every pair of strings satisfying the preconditions, if the function returns r on (initial, target), then when it is invoked on the swapped arguments (target, initial) it also returns r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).

statement: Let revInitial be the slice of length len(initial) with revInitial[i] = initial[len(initial)-1-i] for 0 <= i < len(initial), and let revTarget be defined analogously from target. Whenever the function returns r on (initial, target), any invocation on (revInitial, revTarget) returns the same r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(initial) <= 1000 and 1 <= len(target) <= 1000; every byte of initial and target is an ASCII lowercase letter (code in 97..122 inclusive).
